summary: Radar for 2026-10-22, GLP-1 focus. Two fresh results for named next-generation drugs fit Lane C, and we should act on both now. 1) The full retatrutide sleep apnea trials (TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA) were published in NEJM on Oct 20 and presented at Sleep Europe 2026. At 80 weeks, the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) fell by up to 34.3 events per hour on retatrutide versus 9.9 on placebo. I found no YouTube explainer for it, and retatrutide-named Shorts have a median of 120 views. 2) Novo presented a CagriSema analysis in women from REDEFINE 1 at the Menopause Society meeting (Oct 20–22): 25.0% weight loss versus 3.0% on placebo at 68 weeks, using the efficacy estimand (assumes everyone stayed on treatment). CNBC, Pharmacy Times and Medical Daily have covered it, but creators haven't yet. The FDA decision is expected in Q4 2026. Make the long-form first, then a funnel Short that names it. Lane B (gray-market) is still our strongest repeatable lane. CBS lab-tested vials sold as retatrutide (Oct 21), Australia reports peptide-linked hospital admissions, and Lilly's lawsuits continue. The mainstream recall wave for compounded tirzepatide (Apothecary Pharma: Class II, set Oct 10, coverage Oct 20–22 in USA Today, LA Times, Fox and Good Housekeeping) suits a Lane B long-form, but we've already used this week's recall Short slot. For Lane A, the best fits are side effects (The Conversation's Oct 22 nausea piece is a fresh hook), stopping tirzepatide or semaglutide, and holiday eating ahead of Halloween and Thanksgiving. Lilly's Q3 call on Oct 29 is the next Lane C window. Rejected: the Pharmaceutical Technology 'research-grade retatrutide sourcing checklist' (it explains how to buy) and the low-dose tirzepatide 'strategy' paper (dosing). Handle eye-stroke (NAION), addiction telehealth and cannabis with care. Note: YouTube competition counts are estimates. Search didn't return YouTube listings directly, so 'low' means no creator explainer turned up in web results.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for sleep apnea: full Phase 3 results in NEJM (TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA, published Oct 20, 2026, Sleep Europe 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C first explainer, long-form today or tomorrow at 14:00 with retatrutide first in the title, e.g. 'Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Found'. Explain AHI in plain words (breathing pauses per hour of sleep). Two trials: adults with OSA and obesity or overweight, without type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) and with it (TRIUMPH-2-OSA). Average AHI change at 80 weeks versus placebo, named by trial arm: TRIUMPH-1-OSA −34.3 (9 mg arm) vs −9.9; TRIUMPH-2-OSA −25.4 (12 mg arm) vs −10.3. Put tirzepatide's approved OSA use (SURMOUNT-OSA) alongside as context, labelled indirect, never 'beat'. Status: investigational, not approved anywhere; Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027. Funnel Short at 20:00 naming the long-form. Note: GI side effects, plus the prescriber line.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–7 days (and again when Lilly's Q3 call lands Oct 29)
candidates.why_now: NEJM full publication and congress presentation on Oct 20. Retatrutide-named Shorts are our best performers (median 120). The playbook says to make the Lane C long-form first because the retatrutide T2D result went out as a Short only. Sleep apnea is a body-effect topic that also works on Instagram.

candidates.angle: Lane C long-form with CagriSema first, e.g. 'CagriSema for Women: What the New Menopause Analysis Shows'. About 2,300 women with obesity or overweight: 25.0% vs 3.0% placebo at 68 weeks. By stage (about 1,900 women): premenopausal 26.7%, perimenopausal 24.8%, postmenopausal 23.1%. Say clearly that these are efficacy-estimand figures (assuming everyone stayed on treatment), a post hoc subgroup analysis presented by Novo. Full trial GI events: 79.6% (nausea 55%), mostly mild to moderate. Status: not approved; FDA decision expected Q4 2026. Explain what amylin adds to semaglutide. Avoid 'Did X beat Y?' framing.
